ab: ab, ā (prep. + abl.) — from, away from; by
ac: atque, ac — and, and also (ac before consonants)
accipiunt: accipiō, accipere, accēpī, acceptum — to take in, receive (3rd pl. pres.)
ad: ad (prep. + acc.) — to, toward; at, near
adparet: adpareō (appareō), -ēre, -paruī — to appear, come into view, be visible (3rd sg. pres.)
adsunt: adsum, adesse, adfuī — to be present, be at hand (3 pl. pres.)
aeacidae: Aeacidēs, -ae (m.) — descendant of Aeacus; Achilles, his grandson (gen./dat. sg.)
aeneas: Aenēās, -ae (m.) — Aeneas, Trojan prince, son of Venus and Anchises (nom. sg.)
aequora: aequor, aequoris (n.) — level surface; the sea, the waters (acc./nom. pl.)
aere: aes, aeris (n.) — bronze, copper; bronze prow (abl. sg.) · āēr, āēris (m.) — air, mist, cloud (abl. sg.)
aliae: alius, -a, -ud — other, another; aliae, others (f. nom. pl.)
alta: altus, -a, -um — high; deep (f. nom./abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
amore: amor, amōris (m.) — love, longing, desire (abl. sg.)
amplius: amplius (adv., comp. of amplus) — more, further, longer (n. acc. sg. as adv.)
anchises: Anchīsēs, -ae (m.) — Anchises, Aeneas' father (nom. sg., Greek form)
andromache: Andromachē, -ēs (f.) — Andromache, Hector's wife (nom. sg., Greek form)
animi: animus, -ī (m.) — mind, spirit, courage (gen. sg., loc. animī, "in spirit"; also nom. pl.)
animis: animus, -ī (m.) — mind, spirit, heart; courage, temper (dat./abl. pl.)
ante: ante (prep. + acc., adv.) — before, in front of; previously
apollo: Apollō, -inis (m.) — Apollo, god of prophecy (nom. sg.) · also voc. sg. (pulcher Apollo)
aras: āra, -ae (f.) — altar; the Arae, 'Altars', a reef off Africa (acc. pl.)
arces: arx, arcis (f.) — citadel, stronghold, height (acc./nom. pl.)
argolicas: Argolicus, -a, -um — of Argos, Greek (f. acc. pl.)
arma: arma, -ōrum (n. pl.) — arms, weapons; war (acc./nom. pl.)
armenta: armentum, -ī (n.) — herd, drove (of cattle, deer) (nom./acc. pl.)
armis: arma, -ōrum (n. pl.) — arms, weapons; war (abl./dat. pl.)
auris: auris, -is (f.) — ear (acc. pl., -is for -ēs; also gen. sg.)
casum: cāsus, -ūs (m.) — fall, chance, misfortune, death (acc. sg.)
casus: cāsus, -ūs (m.) — fall; chance, misfortune, disaster (acc./nom. pl.; nom. sg.)
cavata: cavō, -āre — to hollow out (perf. pass. part., f. abl. sg.; f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
certatim: certātim (adv.) — in rivalry, emulously, vying with one another
cessisse: cēdō, -ere, cessī, cessum — to go away, withdraw, yield (perf. inf.)
circumvolat: circumvolō, -āre — to fly around, hover about (3 sg. pres.)
cognoscere: cognoscō, -ere, cognōvī, cognitum — to get to know, learn, recognise (pres. inf.)
compellare: compellō (1), -āre — to address, accost (pres. inf., historical inf.)
condunt: condō, -ere, -didī, -ditum — to put away, hide, store; found (3rd pl. pres.)
considere: cōnsīdō, -ere, -sēdī, -sessum — to sit down, settle (pres. inf.)
cum: cum — (conj.) when, since, although; (prep. + abl.) with
cursum: cursus, -ūs (m.) — running, course, voyage; pursuit (acc. sg.)
curva: curvus, -a, -um — curved, bent, winding (f. abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
curvo: curvus, -a, -um — curved, bent, winding (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
danais: Danaī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Danaans, the Greeks (dat./abl. pl.)
dat: dō, dare, dedī, datum — to give; dat lōra, slackens the reins (3rd sg. pres.)
de: dē (prep. + abl.) — down from, from; concerning
dedere: dō, dare, dedī, datum — to give, give forth (3rd pl. perf. = dedērunt)
deum: deus, -ī (m.) — god (gen. pl., old form = deōrum; also acc. sg.)
di: deus, -ī (m.) — god (nom. pl., contracted dī = deī, diī)
dicta: dīcō, dīcere, dīxī, dictum — to say, speak (perf. pass. part., n. nom./acc. pl.); dictum (n.), word, saying · also f. nom. sg. (coniunx dicta, called)
dira: dīrus, -a, -um — dreadful, ghastly, ill-omened (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
dirae: dīrus, -a, -um — dreadful, dire, grim (f. nom. pl.)
diverso: dīversus, -a, -um — turned different ways, separate, opposed (m. abl. sg.)
dixit: dīcō, -ere, dixī, dictum — to say, speak (3rd sg. perf.)
domus: domus, -ūs (f.) — house, home, dwelling (nom. sg.) · gen. sg. (of the house; domus scelus)
et: et — and; also, even; et… et: both… and
evasisse: ēvādō, -ere, ēvāsī, ēvāsum — to get out, escape, make one's way through (perf. inf., = ēvāsisse)
ex: ex, ē (prep. + abl.) — out of, from
extulit: efferō, efferre, extulī, ēlātum — to lift up, raise (3rd sg. perf.)
fessi: fessus, -a, -um — weary, worn out (m. nom. pl.); fessī rērum, weary of their troubles
foedare: foedō, -āre, -āvī — to defile, disfigure, pollute (pres. inf.)
forte: fors, fortis (f.) — chance, luck; forte, by chance, perhaps (abl. sg. as adverb)
gente: gēns, gentis (f.) — race, people, nation (abl. sg.)
haec: hic, haec, hoc — this; haec (n. pl.), these things, these words (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom. sg.)
hanc: hic, haec, hoc — this (f. acc. sg.)
haud: haud (adv.) — not, by no means (negating a single word)
hectoreum: Hectoreus, -a, -um — of Hector, Hector's (n. nom./acc. sg.; m. acc. sg.)
hic: hīc (adv.) — here; hic, haec, hoc (pron.), this (m. nom. sg.)
hiemps: hiems, hiemis (f.) — winter, storm (nom. sg., old form hiemps)
honores: honor (honōs), honōris (m.) — honour, esteem; offering, sacrifice (nom./acc. pl.)
horrentibus: horreō, -ēre, horruī — to bristle, be rough, shudder (pres. part., m./f./n. abl./dat. pl.)
hostis: hostis, -is (m./f.) — enemy (nom. sg.; acc. pl. in -is = -ēs)
hunc: hic, haec, hoc — this; hunc, this man (m. acc. sg.)
iam: iam (adv.) — now, already; iam… iam, now… now
illis: ille, illa, illud — that, those (m./f./n. abl./dat. pl.)
in: in (prep.) — + acc. into, onto, against; + abl. in, on
indicit: indīcō, -ere, indixī, indictum — to proclaim, appoint, declare (3rd sg. pres.)
infelix: infēlix, -īcis — unlucky, unhappy, ill-starred (m. nom. sg.) · also f. nom. sg. (infēlix Dīdō) · also n. nom./acc. sg. (monstrum infēlix)
inruimus: inruō (irruō), -ere, -ruī — to rush in, charge (1 pl. pres.; also perf.)
insontis: īnsōns, -ontis — guiltless, innocent (gen. sg.; acc. pl., = īnsontēs)
invadunt: invādō, invādere, invāsī, invāsum — to go in, attack, fall upon (3rd pl. pres.)
ipsumque: ipse, ipsa, ipsum — himself, the very (m. acc. sg.; n. nom./acc. sg.) + -que 'and'
italiam: Ītalia, -ae (f.) — Italy (acc. sg.; first syllable long in verse)
iubent: iubeō, -ēre, iussī, iussum — to order, bid, command (3rd pl. pres.)
iubet: iubeō, -ēre, iussī, iussum — to order, bid (3rd sg. pres.)
iussi: iubeō, -ēre, iussī, iussum — to order, bid (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl.)
iuvat: iuvō, -āre, iūvī, iūtum — to help, please; iuvat (impers.), it pleases, it is a joy (3rd sg. pres.)
laeta: laetus, -a, -um — glad, joyful (f. nom. sg.) · also n. nom. pl. (laeta saecula) · also n. acc. pl. (per līmina laeta)
latentia: lateō, latēre, latuī — to lie hidden, lurk (pres. part., n. acc./nom. pl.)
legimus: legō, -ere, lēgī, lectum — to gather; skim, coast along (1st pl. pres.)
longo: longus, -a, -um — long, deep, far-reaching (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
ludis: lūdō, -ere, lūsī, lūsum — to play, mock, deceive (2nd sg. pres.)
magna: magnus, -a, -um — great, large, mighty (f. abl./nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
magnis: magnus, -a, -um — great, large, loud (m. abl. pl.) · also f. abl. pl. (magnīs Mycēnīs) · also m. dat. pl. (moenia magnis, for the great)
magno: magnus, -a, -um — great, large, loud (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
magnum: magnus, -a, -um — great, large, vast (m. acc. sg.; n. nom./acc. sg.)
manus: manus, -ūs (f.) — hand; handiwork (acc. pl.; also nom./gen. sg., nom./voc. pl.)
mea: meus, -a, -um — my, mine (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
medio: medius, -a, -um — middle, in the middle of (m./n. abl./dat. sg.)
mihi: ego, meī — I; mihi, to/for me (dat.)
moenibus: moenia, -ium (n. pl.) — walls, city walls (abl./dat. pl.)
monstrum: mōnstrum, -ī (n.) — portent, monster, ominous thing (acc. sg.)
montis: mōns, montis (m.) — mountain (gen. sg.; also acc. pl., = montēs)
nec: nec, neque — and not, nor; nec… nec, neither… nor
neque: neque (nec) — and not, nor; neque enim, for indeed… not
nova: novus, -a, -um — new, fresh, strange (f. nom./abl. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
numina: nūmen, nūminis (n.) — divine will, divinity, god (nom./acc. pl.)
obstipui: obstipescō, -ere, obstipuī — to be stunned, stand amazed (1st sg. perf.)
odorem: odor, odōris (m.) — smell, scent, fragrance (acc. sg.)
omnia: omnis, -e — all, every; omnia, all things, everything (n. nom./acc. pl.)
ora: ōs, ōris (n.) — mouth, face; pl. faces, features (acc./nom. pl.)
pallida: pallidus, -a, -um — pale, wan (n. acc./nom. pl.; f. nom. sg.)
palmis: palma, -ae (f.) — palm of the hand, hand (abl. pl.)
pando: pandō, -ere, pandī, passum — to spread out, lay open, explain (1st sg. pres.)
passim: passim (adv.) — here and there, everywhere, at random
passis: patior, patī, passus sum — to suffer, endure (perf. part. of deponent, m. dat./abl. pl.) · also pandō, -ere, passum — to spread, loosen (crīnibus passīs, with hair loosened; perf. pass. part., m. abl. pl.)
pater: pater, patris (m.) — father (nom. sg.) · also voc. sg. (pater optume)
patrias: patrius, -a, -um — of one's fathers, native, ancestral (f. acc. pl.)
patrio: patrius, -a, -um — of a father, ancestral, father's (m./n. abl. sg.)
pectore: pectus, pectoris (n.) — breast, chest; heart (abl. sg.)
pecus: pecus, pecudis (n.) — herd, flock, creatures (nom./acc. sg.)
per: per (prep. + acc.) — through, across, throughout; by
petimus: petō, -ere, petīvī, petītum — to seek, make for, ask for (1st pl. pres.)
pios: pius, -a, -um — dutiful, righteous, devout (m. acc. pl.)
portu: portus, -ūs (m.) — harbour, port (abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
portus: portus, -ūs (m.) — harbour, haven (acc. pl.; also nom. sg.)
portusque: portus, -ūs (m.) — harbour, port (acc. pl.; also nom. sg./pl.) + -que, and
primum: prīmus, -a, -um — first; prīmum (adv.), first, at first (n. acc. sg. as adv.)
pro: prō (prep. + abl.) — for, on behalf of; before; instead of
protinus: prōtinus (adv.) — straight on, forthwith, at once
puppes: puppis, -is (f.) — stern of a ship; ship (acc./nom. pl.)
pyrrhi: Pyrrhus, -ī (m.) — Pyrrhus, Achilles' son, also Neoptolemus (gen. sg.)
qua: quā (adv.) — where, by which way; in any way (after sī); also quī/quis, f. abl. sg. · also indef. after sī, any (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.: sī qua nūmina) · also after nē, in any way (nē qua)
quae: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., f. nom. sg.; f./n. nom./acc. pl.) · interrog. adj., what? which? (f. nom. sg.: quae sententia) · also interrog. adj., n. nom. pl. (quae sint ea nūmina)
quam: quī, quae, quod — who, which (rel., f. acc. sg.); quam (adv.), how; than · prius… quam (conj.), before, until · indef. after sī/nē, any, some (f. acc. sg.: si quam) · also interrog. adj., what? which? (f. acc. sg.: quam arcem?)
quas: quī, quae, quod — who, which, what (rel. or interrog., f. acc. pl.)
quem: quī, quae, quod — who, whom (rel. or interrog., m. acc. sg.) · quis, quid after sī, nē — any(one), some(one) (indef., m. acc. sg.: sī quem)
refugit: refugiō, -ere, -fūgī — to flee back, recoil from, shrink from (3rd sg. pres.)
rerum: rēs, reī (f.) — thing, matter; pl. circumstances, fortunes (gen. pl.)
rupe: rūpēs, rūpis (f.) — cliff, crag, rock (abl. sg.)
sacraverat: sacrō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to consecrate, hallow (3rd sg. pluperf.)
secus: secus (adv.) — otherwise; haud secus, not otherwise, just so
sed: sed (conj.) — but; sed enim, but indeed
servate: servō, servāre — to keep, save, preserve (2nd pl. imper.)
sese: sē, sēsē — emphatic reflexive, himself, itself, themselves (acc.)
seu: seu (sīve) — or if; seu… seu, whether… or
sidera: sīdus, sīderis (n.) — star, constellation; pl. the sky (acc./nom. pl.)
simoentis: Simoīs, Simoentis (m.) — the Simois, river of Troy (gen. sg.)
sint: sum, esse, fuī — to be (3rd pl. pres. subj.)
sive: sīve (seu) — or if; sīve… sīve, whether… or
sol: sōl, sōlis (m.) — sun; the Sun-god (nom. sg.)
sollemnis: sollemnis, -e — solemn, ritual, annual; sollemnis sacerdōs, officiating priest (m. nom. sg.)
stant: stō, stāre, stetī, statum — to stand, stand firm (3rd pl. pres.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
subimus: subeō, -īre, -iī, -itum — to go under, enter, approach (1st pl. pres.)
talem: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind (m./f. acc. sg.)
tandem: tandem (adv.) — at length, finally; in questions, pray, I ask
tellure: tellūs, tellūris (f.) — earth, ground, land (abl. sg.)
temptant: temptō (tentō), -āre — to try, attempt, test (3 pl. pres.)
tendunt: tendō, tendere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, strain; to head for, make toward (3rd pl. pres.)
tristia: tristis, -e — grim, sad, bitter (n. acc. pl.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
tumulum: tumulus, -ī (m.) — mound, hillock, burial mound (acc. sg.)
ulixi: Ulixēs, -is (m.) — Ulysses, king of Ithaca (gen. sg. Ulixī; also dat. sg.)
ulla: ūllus, -a, -um — any (f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.); with non, no
una: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (f. abl./nom. sg.); ūnā (adv.), together · also ūnā, adv., once (satis ūnā superque, enough once and more)
urbes: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (nom. pl.; also acc. pl.)
verrunt: verrō, -ere, verrī, versum — to sweep, skim (3rd pl. pres.)
vim: vīs (f.; acc. vim, abl. vī) — force, power, violence (acc. sg.)
virum: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero (acc. sg.; also gen. pl., old form = virōrum)
vobis: tū, tuī — you; vōs, vōbīs, to/for you, by you (dat./abl. pl.)
vocat: vocō, -āre — to call, name, summon (3rd sg. pres.)
vocem: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice, word, sound (acc. sg.)
voltus: vultus (voltus), -ūs (m.) — face, look, expression (nom. sg.; acc. pl.)
vos: tū, vōs — you (2nd pers. pl. pron.) (nom./acc. pl.) · also voc. pl. (vōs, aetērnī ignēs)
vox: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice, word, sound (nom. sg.)
